To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concentrations of Pb, Hg, Cd and As were found in the tissues below EU maximum levels and the FA profiles were similar in both shrimps, but different between species and tissues.
the studied elements were found below the legal limits for consumption, while the FA profiles of the two studied species of shrimp are characterized by high values of DHA, EPA and ω-3 fatty acids.
the levels of Cd, Pb and As in shrimps were higher in the cephalothoraxes than in muscle and the levels of Hg were higher in muscle than in cephalothoraces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comprehensive study of the accumulation of toxic elements and the FA profile of the two most common shrimps in the Mediterranean and the Atlantic.
a nutritional and toxicological assessment of the two shrimps species studied, and the results obtained can provide useful information for the consumer and for the fishery industry.
the assessment of the nutritional value of P. borealis and P. longirostris, which is of great importance for human health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both shrimps are a good source of essential fatty acids, with the advantage of a low level of toxic elements.
the consumption of P. borealis and P. longirostris is nutritionally valuable in terms of essential fatty acids and the toxicological concern of elements’ accumulation is low.
P. longirostris is a better choice for consumption, due to its high nutritional value and the low levels of toxic elements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shrimps are good sources of EPA and DHA, and the ω-6/ω-3 ratio is low, indicating that shrimps are a good source of essential fatty acids.
P. longirostris, in terms of FA, is a good source of EPA and DHA, while P. borealis is rich in ω-3 FA.
both species studied are a source of ω-3 fatty acids with low concentrations of toxic elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumption of shrimps can be a valuable source of ω-3 PUFAs and, at the same time, can be considered a safe food in terms of toxic element contamination.
P. longirostris is a good source of essential fatty acids, especially DHA, EPA and ω-3 fatty acids.
the Mediterranean and northern shrimps are valuable sources of essential fatty acids.
